title: Midday kernel dig + to-dos (Tess)
body:
2026-03-12 midday scratchpad - trying to capture the headspace and next steps for the tail-latency jitter we've been seeing

Context:
- Regression appeared after recent batching changes + small-hot-requests optimization (patch applied last week, rollout-candidate).
- Symptoms: 95/99/99.9p spikes for short requests (seq_len <= 8 tokens) in hosted envs; median unchanged.
- Spike duration: bursts lasting ~30-120s, not correlated with traffic bursts.
- Affected pools: gpu-pool-04, gpu-pool-07; not observed on dedicated-dev nodes.

Observations (recent traces + logs):
- Flamegraphs show unexpected user->kernel transitions at tail; syscalls cluster around futex/wake and epoll_wait.
- perf samples show a cluster of samples in a small loop touching a large contiguous mmap (KV cache arena).
- dmesg and node-level metrics show increased softirq preemption in the same windows.
- P50/P90 throughput per worker steady; worker thread schedule gaps ~2-5ms at 99.9p.
- Heap/alloc patterns: small frequent allocations when seq_len small (per-token buffers + ephemeral context structs).

Hypotheses (ordered):
1) False-sharing or mis-aligned cachelines in the KV cache arena cause occasional cross-core contention visible as short preemption spikes for small requests.
   - Rationale: short requests touch different offsets in kv arrays; small requests excite hot-set buckets -> neighboring cores hitting same cachelines.
2) Futex wake contention between runtime thread and a background GC/evictor thread during tight loops for tiny requests.
   - Rationale: logs show wake/futex skewed during spikes.
3) Epoll edge cases where the I/O thread stalls while waiting on completion queue if threads are starved due to kernel scheduler priorities after recent batching change.

Quick experiments to try (fast, low-risk):
- Reproduce locally with a synthetic load that sends 1-4 token requests at 5–20 QPS per worker for 5 minutes; record perf + heatmaps.
  Command: ./scripts/run-synthetic.sh --seq-lens 1,2,4 --qps 10 --duration 300 --collect perf,flame
- Force cacheline alignment of KV arena at 64B boundaries in a debug build and run stress test. (toggle via runtime flag kv_arena_align=64)
- Insert lightweight per-core padding in KV slot struct to test false-sharing (debug build).
- Add a cheap tracing probe (eBPF tracepoint) on futex/wake to correlate futex events with tail spikes (low overhead).

Longer experiments (if quick ones suggest alignment):
- Run a canary with kv_arena_align=64 on gpu-pool-04 for a day, monitor 99.9p.
- Run futex metrics (histogram) in prod for 24h under controlled traffic.

Immediate TODOs (next 48h):
- [ ] Wire up synthetic test harness for tiny requests (priority: high) (owner: me)
- [ ] Add eBPF futex/wake probe on dev nodes (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Build a debug binary with kv padding flag, smoke on staging (owner: Tess)
- [ ] Post initial findings to #serving-runtime and add a short blurb to the incident doc (owner: Tess)
- [ ] Create JIRA INF-3498 to track kv alignment canary (owner: Tess)

Notes from pairing with Maya (morning):
- She suggested instrumenting per-thread runloop latencies and correlating with the batching window start/stop timings (good idea).
- We saw one instance where two workers on same host had mirrored 2–3ms gaps — suspicious for scheduler noise.

Quick command snippets / reminders:
- Capture perf: sudo perf record -F 199 -a -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf script | ./scripts/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./scripts/flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
- Snapshot threads: for pid $PID, run: sudo perf sched record -p $PID -o sched.data -- sleep 30; sudo perf sched report -i sched.data
- eBPF futex probe (one-liner): sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_futex { @[comm] = count(); }'

Open questions (need quick answers):
- Does the batching change alter thread-affinity or pinning? I thought we left core pinning as-is. (check PR #1892)
- Any kernel updates in the last node image push for gpu-pool-04? (ask infra)

Random quick wins if time allows:
- Add tiny randomized jitter to per-request timers to break sync storms (cheap, reversible).
- Add per-host futex-wake rate as an SLI and surface in console rollups for the last 7 days.

Decision boundaries (how we'll decide root cause):
- If alignment/padding build eliminates 99.9p spikes in staging synthetic runs -> false sharing likely -> plan remediation and canary rollout.
- If futex probes show wake storms aligning with spikes -> restructure evictor design to avoid hot wakes or use lockless notification.
- If both negative, dig deeper into kernel scheduling (submit a kernel-qa ticket and involve SRE).

Log append (raw captures to attach later):
- perf-raw-2026-03-12-10:23: uid 432s sample set (saved to /tmp/perf-432.raw)
- sched-record-03_12.trace

End notes: keep this lightweight. Aim to have reproducible test + first debug build by end of day tomorrow. If I hit a blocker on the eBPF probe, loop in Diego early.

-- Tess
